children: The European Union wants to give national and local authorities legal clarity to curb short-term property rentals, as cities popular with tourists look for ways to contain rising housing costs.
EU competition commissioner Teresa Ribera said in a statement on Wednesday that the 27-member bloc faces a "terrible crisis" preventing many citizens from accessing housing.

While the so-called Affordable Housing Act does not restrict short-term rentals itself, the European Commission--the bloc's executive arm--wants to set up a framework regional authorities can use to assess areas that are under "housing stress" due to tourist rentals before they take proportionate measures to address that.

Europeans have struggled with rising house prices across the bloc for years, which some residents in popular tourist hot spots attribute to the proliferation of homes listed on platforms such as Airbnb in their cities.
Some bodies have already taken action. In Barcelona, a city that drew some 16 million visitors last year, the municipal government has moved to eliminate short-term rentals by 2028.
"With the Affordable Housing Act, we are providing legal certainty to local authorities, enabling them to take action and address one of the biggest problems of our time," Ribera said.
